summary: I and II both cover agricultural earth covering: watermelons appear with I in JTM 1.1/5 and II in JL 7.8/5–6. The evidence does not demonstrate a semantic stem split. Seed/cutting, corpse, live person, money, faeces and grave objects retain the same earth-covering sense.

Concealment without earth is grouped as one new I.2; bridal face covering is not a separate technical sense. Shame hiding and captive hiding share concealment, while head concealment receives an idiomatic phrase for its recurrent-body-part style, provisional on one attestation.

Detransitive examples show eventive earth covering and resulting hidden states without an expressed agent. The absent Detransitive sense list is supplied as 1, covering the inherited boxes. Snow coverage at 91/37 provisionally supplies ko-Preterit, with morphology flagged for checking.
Reflexive ruḥe at 95/163 co-occurs with an actual pit, hay and earth, so it is active physical self-burial. Grammatical reflexivity alone does not establish Detransitive.

No matches were found for ḥfar w or ṭməlle qarʕe by glossary lookup. New idioms are proposed only under this root; no linked ḥfr file is edited. Existing JL, PrS 126/8, Ritter and LB references are not duplicated.

The reader’s ṭəmrituwo Preterit-wa label is corrected to Infectum-wa on the subject-before-wo pattern; the expected active Preterit would have an l-agent. Do not create a new box from an English past paraphrase.

Round 1 already establishes I concealment without earth as sense 2 and I Detransitive hidden/buried as 1. Neither is proposed again. The new II Detransitive mystery has an affected/experiencer -le, not an overt agent.
The theological rozo/sər context is a literary/religious participant extension of concealment; it does not demonstrate an independent active II abstract sense.

Confirm koṭmiro at 91/37 as feminine Detransitive ko-Preterit versus an irregular adjective; the entry's ṭmiro at 24/194 also allows a finite/participial ambiguity and is retained as inherited Part. Pass.
Does the shame gesture in MAC Xalaf Agha/58 conventionally mean bowing the head or physically concealing it? The proposal says verbergen and does not impose a gesture mechanism.
For JL 10.11/5, does -e refer to the seed strip or seed? For 108/38–39, does the feminine object refer to field, furrow or a ploughing pass? The agricultural referent remains unresolved.
Confirm dismissive ḥfar w ṭmar as a conventional expression and whether a cross-reference should also be added under ḥfr.
Jan 2.2/186: confirm ṭəmrituwo as I Infectum-wa 2pl, rather than a local Preterit-wa formation; the -itu before -wo motivates the provisional correction.

Jan 2.31/4863: is -le the affected experiencer, a recipient or a possessor of the mystery? Does kmiṭamərle imply ongoing hiding or inaccessible understanding? Only the attested Detransitive Infectum is added.
